method: Versions and licences come from the npm registry (/-/package/<name>/dist-tags, then /<name>/<version>). Each tarball was downloaded to scratch and walked with deps.fetch's filter (SOURCE_EXTS, <=2 MB) and then index_code.iter_files' filter (SKIP_DIRS includes dist and build, <=1.5 MB). bytes_index_code_walks_by_default is what a plain `index_code.py <src>` would read. est_chunks is a range scaled from the two held indexes (1,180 to 2,895 chunks per MB) and is an estimate, not a measurement. For every package, the registry dist.tarball equals the URL deps.fetch builds.

how_the_repo_indexes_a_package.automatic: packages.ensure_for(root) is called from proxy.complete() for every request that resolves a repo root. It takes deps.plan(root): packages that are BOTH imported >=2 times in the repo's .ts/.js AND pinned in its lockfile, up to 25. For each one without an index it calls deps.fetch(name, version), which unpacks the npm tarball to index/packages/_src/<slug>@<ver>, then runs scripts/index_code.py <src> in a background thread with CODE_INDEX_DB=deps.db_path(name, version) and INDEX_NO_EMBED=1. There is no CLI that takes a package name. `python mcp/deps.py <repo>` and `python mcp/packages.py <repo>` only PRINT the plan.
how_the_repo_indexes_a_package.no_embed_means: INDEX_NO_EMBED=1 makes embed_batch return zero vectors WITHOUT counting them as dead, so check_alive passes. The result serves the symbol table and BM25 (enough for held_sources(), which counts chunks > 0) but has no embedding arm for find_by_meaning. The two held indexes were NOT built that way: 200/200 sampled vectors in each are non-zero, i.e. rebuilt with embeddings.
operator_command_git_bash: # with embeddings (needs the embedding server at LLAMA_STACK_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:11434, model 'embeddings'; refuses to write if >2% of vectors are dead):
# or exactly what ensure_for does (no GPU, zero vectors):
how_the_repo_indexes_a_package.extra_roots: index_code.py accepts several roots, and a root may be a directory or a single file. The walk prunes SKIP_DIRS (dist, build, ...) only BELOW a root, so naming dist/... explicitly is the way to index a dist-only package without editing code. Packages listed without extra_roots index correctly by default.
how_the_repo_indexes_a_package.picked_up_by: domains.held_sources() (cached on the store's name/mtime/size listing, no restart) and packages.catalogue()/indexed_versions(). The file is index/packages/<slug>@<version>.sqlite3, slug = name without '@', '/' -> '__'.

defect_found: packages.ensure_for runs index_code.py on the tarball root, and index_code.SKIP_DIRS contains 'dist' and 'build'. Any dist-only package therefore auto-indexes as little more than its README, yet held_sources() counts it as held because chunks > 0 (PROTOCOL rule 1 shape: present, not working). Measured: @react-three/fiber@10.0.0-alpha.5 walks 9,372 of 4,683,801 fetched bytes, @webgpu/types 4,815 of 122,628, postprocessing 8,384 of 2,526,387, wgpu-matrix 13,595 of 631,299. fiber@9.8.0 walks 453,917 bytes, mostly a vendored react-reconciler. Not fixed here (read-only task).
domains_gap: domains.PACKAGE_DOMAINS has no entry for @react-three/postprocessing, postprocessing, wgpu-matrix, @types/three, @typegpu/three, @typegpu/noise, type-fest or three-mesh-bvh, and HELD_ALIASES only knows three, typegpu, fiber, drei and koota. Held packages are still matched by bare name in domains._named.

packages.name: @react-three/fiber
packages.why: Current stable R3F. Every r3f.jsonl recipe cites its API, but the server holds none of its source.
packages.notes: The tarball is dist-only. The default walk indexes 454 KB, of which 377 KB is a VENDORED react-reconciler, so a default index answers R3F questions out of React internals. Pass the esm bundle and declarations as extra roots and skip the cjs/prod duplicates.

packages.name: @react-three/fiber
packages.why: The v10 line that r3f.jsonl's v10 recipes (CHANGELOG-ALPHA, frame-loop, webgpu/*) describe. It is the version-sensitive one.
packages.notes: Only 10 source files, all under dist/, so the default walk keeps just the README (9 KB). Each bundle ships cjs/mjs/legacy triplicates, so index the .mjs and .d.ts only. A better alternative is the v10 branch of github.com/pmndrs/react-three-fiber (packages/fiber/src) as a repo index, the way koota is held.

packages.name: @react-three/drei
packages.why: The drei release paired with fiber 9. r3f.jsonl has about 25 drei recipes and no source behind them.
packages.notes: Layout is fine: core/ and web/ sit at the package root, so all 1.75 MB is walked.

packages.name: @react-three/drei
packages.why: The drei release paired with fiber v10 (webgpu/ and legacy/ entry points). r3f.jsonl cites MIGRATION_V10_TO_V11.
packages.notes: Layout is fine (all 2.96 MB walked). legacy/, webgpu/ and native/ are parallel builds, so expect near-duplicate chunks.

packages.name: @types/three
packages.why: The .d.ts surface of three, including TSL node typings. It answers typing questions that three's JS source cannot, and sits squarely in both the TS-types and three domains.
packages.notes: Pair it with three@0.186.0. Its dist-tags map ts5.6-ts6.0 to 0.186.0.

packages.name: three
packages.why: The held index is 0.185.1. Versions are identities here (deps.py), so a 0.186 user gets a flagged near-miss until this exists.
packages.notes: deps.fetch drops build/three.webgpu.js and three.webgpu.nodes.js (>2 MB) and index_code skips build/. Only src/ and examples/ are indexed, which is the intended outcome. Expect about 15k chunks, like 0.185.1.

packages.name: typegpu
packages.why: Already held, and still the latest release. No action needed.

packages.name: @typegpu/three
packages.why: The TypeGPU-to-TSL bridge (pairs with the typegpu_three recipe candidate). Small.

packages.name: @react-three/postprocessing
packages.why: The R3F post-processing wrapper (EffectComposer, effect components). It ships src/, so it indexes cleanly.
packages.notes: Of 391 KB fetched, 279 KB is walked (src/ + root). dist/ duplicates are skipped.

packages.name: postprocessing
packages.why: The effect library under @react-three/postprocessing. The EffectPass/Effect/BlendFunction API lives here.
packages.notes: Licence is Zlib, which is permissive. build/-only tarball: the default walk keeps 8 KB (README + LICENSE). Skip index.cjs, postprocessing.js and the .min duplicates.

packages.name: wgpu-matrix
packages.why: The WebGPU math library that the TypeGPU docs integrate with (integration/working-with-wgpu-matrix). Column-major layout conventions differ from gl-matrix.
packages.notes: dist-only. The default walk keeps the README (13.6 KB).

packages.name: @webgpu/types
packages.why: The canonical WebGPU IDL typings (GPUDevice, GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry, ...). They are the ground truth for the raw-WebGPU recipes in web_gpu.jsonl.
packages.notes: Licence is BSD-3-Clause. The package is one 118 KB .d.ts under dist/, so the default walk keeps only the README (4.8 KB).

packages.name: koota
packages.why: Already searchable as a REPO index (index/repos/koota-6955afb4.sqlite3, which served 116/356 retrieval rows). A package index would add version identity and make held_sources() report it.
packages.notes: Licence is ISC. dist/ holds hashed chunk files (chunk-*.js, types-*.d.ts), so the extra roots must be re-read from the fetched tree per version. The repo index is the better source.

packages.name: type-fest
packages.why: The reference implementation of advanced TS type patterns (Tagged, DistributedOmit, ...). typescript_types.jsonl already cites its source files.
packages.notes: The licence is the SPDX expression (MIT OR CC0-1.0). source/*.d.ts is walked in full.

packages.name: three-mesh-bvh
packages.why: The BVH raycast acceleration behind drei's <Bvh>, and a common R3F performance fix.
packages.notes: src/ (476 KB, the real source) is walked in full. The skipped build/ is only bundled duplicates, so the default index is complete.
